name: Deer in the Headlights
description: A primary mover cannot move while its origin square is attacked by an opponent piece.
ambiguities: Attacked means pseudo-attacked in the current position, including pinned attackers. Castling is evaluated by the primary king origin, not its auxiliary rook.

name: Jumpy
description: If any attacked piece has an ordinary legal move, the affected player must move an attacked piece.
ambiguities: An attacked but immobile piece does not trigger the rule because possible is evaluated over ordinary legal moves.

name: Medusa
description: A primary mover attacked along an unobstructed line by an opponent queen cannot move.
ambiguities: Queen attacks are pseudo-attacks in the current position; blockers of either color stop the ray.

name: Stand Your Ground
description: A primary mover may capture only when its origin square is attacked by an opponent piece.
ambiguities: Attacked means pseudo-attacked before the move. En-passant and capturing promotion are captures.

name: Unrequited Love
description: The king cannot increase its distance to the nearest own queen, and an own queen cannot move closer to the own king.
ambiguities: Distance is Manhattan and equal distance is permitted. With multiple queens, king distance uses the nearest own queen; the singular public wording does not define promoted queens.

name: Helicopter Parent
description: The affected player loses if any own pawn is not defended by another own piece.
ambiguities: Defended means pseudo-defended in the current position. A player with no pawns has no undefended pawn and does not lose.

name: Paranoid
description: The affected player loses if their king is not defended by another own piece.
ambiguities: Defense is evaluated as pseudo-attack of the current king square rather than a simulated legal recapture after king removal.

name: Rook Buddies
description: Rooks and castling are locked until two own rooks have shared an unobstructed rank or file.
ambiguities: Any pair of own rooks, including promoted rooks, can unlock permanently. Castling is locked because it moves an auxiliary rook.

name: Atomic Bomb
description: The affected player loses after the opponent captures a piece whose capture square was adjacent to the affected king.
ambiguities: For en-passant, adjacency uses the removed pawn square rather than the capturing pawn landing square.

name: Get Down Mr. President
description: While in check, the affected player's primary king cannot move.
ambiguities: Implemented relative to standard-check legality; the source game's capturable-king model may allow positions that standard chess rejects.

name: Guerilla Tactics
description: After an affected-player capture, the same physical piece must return to its previous origin if an ordinary legal return is available.
ambiguities: A capturing promotion is followed through its promoted type. If the piece is captured or cannot return, the obligation is inactive.

name: Prince Charming
description: If any own queen is attacked and a knight has an ordinary legal move, the affected player must move a knight.
ambiguities: Any promoted own queen can trigger. A pawn promotion to knight remains a pawn primary move and does not satisfy.

name: Savior Complex
description: While in check, every legal response must use a primary queen mover.
ambiguities: A pawn promotion to queen is a pawn move. An empty filtered set produces the generic drawback loss. Implemented relative to standard-check legality; the source game's capturable-king model may differ.

name: Shellshocked
description: After an opponent capture, affected-player pieces adjacent to the captured piece's square cannot move for one turn.
ambiguities: For en-passant the blast center is the removed pawn square. Castling is forbidden if either the king or auxiliary rook origin is frozen.

name: Skittish
description: While in check, every legal response must use the primary king.
ambiguities: Implemented relative to standard-check legality. An empty filtered set produces the generic drawback loss.

name: Sleepy King
description: The primary king can move only while the affected player is in check.
ambiguities: Being in check permits but does not force a king move. Castling is a king move and is forbidden while not in check. Implemented relative to standard-check legality; the source game's capturable-king model may differ.

name: Three Check
description: The affected player loses after the opponent has delivered three checks.
ambiguities: Check count relies on complete chess.js SAN history ending in + or #. Checkmate SAN counts, and drawback loss is evaluated before standard ending conditions. Midgame initialization with truncated history necessarily undercounts prior checks.
